--- file:///.src/manualMetricTapToTrack.ts ---
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics manualMetricTapToTrack:warning
import * as Fx from "effect/Effect"
import * as M from "effect/Metric"
import { Effect, Metric, pipe, Stream } from "effect"

const responseSize = Metric.gauge("response_size")
const requestErrors = Metric.counter("request_errors")
const requestDefects = Metric.counter("request_defects")
const rpcSuccesses = Metric.counter("rpc_successes")
const userCount = Metric.gauge("user_count")
const errorsByTag = Metric.frequency("errors_by_tag")
const defectsSeen = Metric.frequency("defects_seen")
const bigintGauge = Metric.gauge("bigint_gauge", { bigint: true })
const metrics = { requests: Metric.counter("requests") }
let mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter")

type Failure = { readonly _tag: "NotFound" } | { readonly _tag: "Timeout" }

declare const handleRequest: Effect.Effect<number, Error>
declare const fetchUsers: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>, Failure>
declare const failsWithString: Effect.Effect<number, string>
declare const bigintEffect: Effect.Effect<bigint>
declare const computeSize: () => number
declare const metricFor: (tag: string) => Metric.Metric<number, Metric.CounterState<number>>

// MUST TRIGGER: issue example, tap / tapError / tapDefect each only update one metric
// tap -> Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize) (input is the parameter verbatim)
// tapError -> Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1) (unused parameter, constant input)
// tapDefect -> Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1)
export const issueExample = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.trackSuccesses(responseSize),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.tap direct-effect overload (Effect-TS/effect rpc-schemas fixture)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const directEffect = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with a computed input; the input is evaluated
// once when the pipeline is built in both spellings, so withConstantInput keeps that
export const directEffectComputedInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with an inline metric; it is built once in both spellings
export const directEffectInlineMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(Metric.counter("inline_successes"), 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: input is an expression of the parameter -> mapper overload
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, (users) => users.length)
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag, (error) => error._tag)
export const mapperInput = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap((users) => Metric.update(userCount, users.length)),
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error._tag))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: tapError / tapDefect with the parameter as the input verbatim
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag) / Effect.trackDefects(defectsSeen, ...)
export const errorVerbatim = failsWithString.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error))
)
export const defectMapped = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapDefect((defect) => Metric.update(defectsSeen, String(defect)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: constant input computed per run; the mapper form keeps per-run evaluation
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, () => computeSize())
export const perRunConstantInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: ignored but named parameter
export const ignoredParameter = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((_) => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: destructured parameter; the mapper keeps the parameter list
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, ({ length }) => length)
export const destructuredParameter = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap(({ length }) => Metric.update(userCount, length))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: bigint gauge fed with the success value verbatim
export const bigintVerbatim = bigintEffect.pipe(
  Effect.tap((value) => Metric.update(bigintGauge, value))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: block body with a single return of the metric update
export const blockBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    return Metric.update(responseSize, size)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: function expression callback
export const functionExpression = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapError(function() {
    return Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized callback body
export const parenthesizedBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => (Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe function form
export const piped = pipe(handleRequest, Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first forms (callback and direct effect)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(handleRequest, responseSize)
export const dataFirst = Effect.tap(handleRequest, (size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const dataFirstDirect = Effect.tap(handleRequest, Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const dataFirstError = Effect.tapError(handleRequest, () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-last form applied directly
export const dataLast = Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))(handleRequest)

// MUST TRIGGER: aliased module imports for both Effect and Metric
export const aliasedModules = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.tap((size) => M.update(responseSize, size)),
  Fx.tapDefect(() => M.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the API references are hidden behind const aliases
const tapAlias = Effect.tap
const updateAlias = Metric.update
export const aliasedApis = handleRequest.pipe(tapAlias((size) => updateAlias(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable arguments of Effect.fn
export const tracedHandler = Effect.fn("tracedHandler")(
  function*(id: string) {
    return id.length
  },
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: only the metric tap in a longer chain is reported
export const chained = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.map((size) => size * 2),
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.log(size))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a function body, with module-level metrics declared before it
export function nestedScope() {
  return handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already using the track* combinators
export const alreadyTracked = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize),
  Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1),
  Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1),
  Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the callback does more than update one metric
export const alsoLogs = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.log(size))))
)
export const sequencedUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Effect.andThen(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1), Metric.update(userCount, 1)))
)
export const allUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.all([Metric.update(responseSize, size), Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)]))
)
export const delayedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.delay("1 second")))
)
export const multiStatementBlock = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    const doubled = size * 2
    return Metric.update(responseSize, doubled)
  })
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is conditional
export const conditionalUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => size > 0 ? Metric.update(responseSize, size) : Effect.void)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is wrapped in another effect constructor
export const suspendedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.suspend(() => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric depends on the callback parameter
export const metricFromError = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(metricFor(error._tag), 1))
)
export const metricWithErrorAttributes = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(Metric.withAttributes(requestErrors, { tag: error._tag }), 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: inside a callback the metric expression is evaluated on every run;
// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(metrics.requests, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric is declared after the call; the lazy callback reads it
// later, but track* would read it while it is still in the TDZ
export const laterMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(declaredLater, 1))
)
const declaredLater = Metric.counter("declared_later")

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Metric.modify adds a delta and is not what track* calls
export const modifyGauge = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.modify(userCount, size))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: reading a metric value is not an update
export const readMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.value(responseSize))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: data-last Metric.update is out of scope; only the data-first call is matched
export const dataLastUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => responseSize.pipe(Metric.update(size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the direct effect is a precomputed update, not an inline Metric.update call
const precomputedUpdate = Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)
export const precomputedDirect = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(precomputedUpdate))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free callback, not an inline metric update
const recordSize = (size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)
export const pointFree = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(recordSize))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: tap variants without a track* counterpart
export const tapCause = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapCause(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
export const tapErrorTag = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapErrorTag("NotFound", () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)
export const onExit = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.onExit(() => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.tap is a different API
export const streamTap = Stream.make(1, 2, 3).pipe(Stream.tap((n) => Metric.update(responseSize, n)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: unrelated tap/update APIs with the same shape
const unrelated = {
  tap: <A>(f: (a: A) => unknown) => f,
  update: (_metric: unknown, _input: number) => Effect.void
}
export const unrelatedTap = unrelated.tap((size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const unrelatedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap((size) => unrelated.update(responseSize, size)))

void (mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter_2"))

// MUST TRIGGER: aliased module imports for both Effect and Metric
export const aliasedModules = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.tap((size) => M.update(responseSize, size)),
  Fx.tapDefect(() => M.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the API references are hidden behind const aliases
const tapAlias = Effect.tap
const updateAlias = Metric.update
export const aliasedApis = handleRequest.pipe(tapAlias((size) => updateAlias(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable arguments of Effect.fn
export const tracedHandler = Effect.fn("tracedHandler")(
  function*(id: string) {
    return id.length
  },
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: only the metric tap in a longer chain is reported
export const chained = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.map((size) => size * 2),
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.log(size))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a function body, with module-level metrics declared before it
export function nestedScope() {
  return handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already using the track* combinators
export const alreadyTracked = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize),
  Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1),
  Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1),
  Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the callback does more than update one metric
export const alsoLogs = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.log(size))))
)
export const sequencedUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Effect.andThen(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1), Metric.update(userCount, 1)))
)
export const allUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.all([Metric.update(responseSize, size), Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)]))
)
export const delayedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.delay("1 second")))
)
export const multiStatementBlock = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    const doubled = size * 2
    return Metric.update(responseSize, doubled)
  })
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is conditional
export const conditionalUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => size > 0 ? Metric.update(responseSize, size) : Effect.void)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is wrapped in another effect constructor
export const suspendedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.suspend(() => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric depends on the callback parameter
export const metricFromError = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(metricFor(error._tag), 1))
)
export const metricWithErrorAttributes = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(Metric.withAttributes(requestErrors, { tag: error._tag }), 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: inside a callback the metric expression is evaluated on every run;
// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(metrics.requests, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric is declared after the call; the lazy callback reads it
// later, but track* would read it while it is still in the TDZ
export const laterMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(declaredLater, 1))
)
const declaredLater = Metric.counter("declared_later")

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Metric.modify adds a delta and is not what track* calls
export const modifyGauge = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.modify(userCount, size))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: reading a metric value is not an update
export const readMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.value(responseSize))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: data-last Metric.update is out of scope; only the data-first call is matched
export const dataLastUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => responseSize.pipe(Metric.update(size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the direct effect is a precomputed update, not an inline Metric.update call
const precomputedUpdate = Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)
export const precomputedDirect = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(precomputedUpdate))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free callback, not an inline metric update
const recordSize = (size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)
export const pointFree = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(recordSize))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: tap variants without a track* counterpart
export const tapCause = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapCause(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
export const tapErrorTag = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapErrorTag("NotFound", () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)
export const onExit = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.onExit(() => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.tap is a different API
export const streamTap = Stream.make(1, 2, 3).pipe(Stream.tap((n) => Metric.update(responseSize, n)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: unrelated tap/update APIs with the same shape
const unrelated = {
  tap: <A>(f: (a: A) => unknown) => f,
  update: (_metric: unknown, _input: number) => Effect.void
}
export const unrelatedTap = unrelated.tap((size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const unrelatedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap((size) => unrelated.update(responseSize, size)))

void (mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter_2"))

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics manualMetricTapToTrack:warning
import * as Fx from "effect/Effect"
import * as M from "effect/Metric"
import { Effect, Metric, pipe, Stream } from "effect"

const responseSize = Metric.gauge("response_size")
const requestErrors = Metric.counter("request_errors")
const requestDefects = Metric.counter("request_defects")
const rpcSuccesses = Metric.counter("rpc_successes")
const userCount = Metric.gauge("user_count")
const errorsByTag = Metric.frequency("errors_by_tag")
const defectsSeen = Metric.frequency("defects_seen")
const bigintGauge = Metric.gauge("bigint_gauge", { bigint: true })
const metrics = { requests: Metric.counter("requests") }
let mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter")

type Failure = { readonly _tag: "NotFound" } | { readonly _tag: "Timeout" }

declare const handleRequest: Effect.Effect<number, Error>
declare const fetchUsers: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>, Failure>
declare const failsWithString: Effect.Effect<number, string>
declare const bigintEffect: Effect.Effect<bigint>
declare const computeSize: () => number
declare const metricFor: (tag: string) => Metric.Metric<number, Metric.CounterState<number>>

// MUST TRIGGER: issue example, tap / tapError / tapDefect each only update one metric
// tap -> Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize) (input is the parameter verbatim)
// tapError -> Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1) (unused parameter, constant input)
// tapDefect -> Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1)
export const issueExample = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)),
  Fx.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1)
)

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.tap direct-effect overload (Effect-TS/effect rpc-schemas fixture)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const directEffect = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with a computed input; the input is evaluated
// once when the pipeline is built in both spellings, so withConstantInput keeps that
export const directEffectComputedInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with an inline metric; it is built once in both spellings
export const directEffectInlineMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(Metric.counter("inline_successes"), 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: input is an expression of the parameter -> mapper overload
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, (users) => users.length)
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag, (error) => error._tag)
export const mapperInput = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap((users) => Metric.update(userCount, users.length)),
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error._tag))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: tapError / tapDefect with the parameter as the input verbatim
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag) / Effect.trackDefects(defectsSeen, ...)
export const errorVerbatim = failsWithString.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error))
)
export const defectMapped = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapDefect((defect) => Metric.update(defectsSeen, String(defect)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: constant input computed per run; the mapper form keeps per-run evaluation
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, () => computeSize())
export const perRunConstantInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: ignored but named parameter
export const ignoredParameter = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((_) => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: destructured parameter; the mapper keeps the parameter list
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, ({ length }) => length)
export const destructuredParameter = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap(({ length }) => Metric.update(userCount, length))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: bigint gauge fed with the success value verbatim
export const bigintVerbatim = bigintEffect.pipe(
  Effect.tap((value) => Metric.update(bigintGauge, value))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: block body with a single return of the metric update
export const blockBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    return Metric.update(responseSize, size)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: function expression callback
export const functionExpression = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapError(function() {
    return Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized callback body
export const parenthesizedBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => (Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe function form
export const piped = pipe(handleRequest, Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first forms (callback and direct effect)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(handleRequest, responseSize)
export const dataFirst = Effect.tap(handleRequest, (size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const dataFirstDirect = Effect.tap(handleRequest, Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const dataFirstError = Effect.tapError(handleRequest, () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-last form applied directly
export const dataLast = Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))(handleRequest)

// MUST TRIGGER: aliased module imports for both Effect and Metric
export const aliasedModules = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.tap((size) => M.update(responseSize, size)),
  Fx.tapDefect(() => M.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the API references are hidden behind const aliases
const tapAlias = Effect.tap
const updateAlias = Metric.update
export const aliasedApis = handleRequest.pipe(tapAlias((size) => updateAlias(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable arguments of Effect.fn
export const tracedHandler = Effect.fn("tracedHandler")(
  function*(id: string) {
    return id.length
  },
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: only the metric tap in a longer chain is reported
export const chained = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.map((size) => size * 2),
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.log(size))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a function body, with module-level metrics declared before it
export function nestedScope() {
  return handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already using the track* combinators
export const alreadyTracked = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize),
  Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1),
  Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1),
  Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the callback does more than update one metric
export const alsoLogs = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.log(size))))
)
export const sequencedUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Effect.andThen(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1), Metric.update(userCount, 1)))
)
export const allUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.all([Metric.update(responseSize, size), Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)]))
)
export const delayedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.delay("1 second")))
)
export const multiStatementBlock = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    const doubled = size * 2
    return Metric.update(responseSize, doubled)
  })
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is conditional
export const conditionalUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => size > 0 ? Metric.update(responseSize, size) : Effect.void)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is wrapped in another effect constructor
export const suspendedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.suspend(() => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric depends on the callback parameter
export const metricFromError = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(metricFor(error._tag), 1))
)
export const metricWithErrorAttributes = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(Metric.withAttributes(requestErrors, { tag: error._tag }), 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: inside a callback the metric expression is evaluated on every run;
// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(metrics.requests, 1))
)

)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: inside a callback the metric expression is evaluated on every run;
// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(metrics.requests, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric is declared after the call; the lazy callback reads it
// later, but track* would read it while it is still in the TDZ
export const laterMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(declaredLater, 1))
)
const declaredLater = Metric.counter("declared_later")

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Metric.modify adds a delta and is not what track* calls
export const modifyGauge = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.modify(userCount, size))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: reading a metric value is not an update
export const readMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.value(responseSize))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: data-last Metric.update is out of scope; only the data-first call is matched
export const dataLastUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => responseSize.pipe(Metric.update(size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the direct effect is a precomputed update, not an inline Metric.update call
const precomputedUpdate = Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)
export const precomputedDirect = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(precomputedUpdate))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free callback, not an inline metric update
const recordSize = (size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)
export const pointFree = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(recordSize))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: tap variants without a track* counterpart
export const tapCause = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapCause(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
export const tapErrorTag = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapErrorTag("NotFound", () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)
export const onExit = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.onExit(() => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.tap is a different API
export const streamTap = Stream.make(1, 2, 3).pipe(Stream.tap((n) => Metric.update(responseSize, n)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: unrelated tap/update APIs with the same shape
const unrelated = {
  tap: <A>(f: (a: A) => unknown) => f,
  update: (_metric: unknown, _input: number) => Effect.void
}
export const unrelatedTap = unrelated.tap((size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const unrelatedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap((size) => unrelated.update(responseSize, size)))

void (mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter_2"))

--- file:///.src/manualMetricTapToTrack.ts ---
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics manualMetricTapToTrack:warning
import * as Fx from "effect/Effect"
import * as M from "effect/Metric"
import { Effect, Metric, pipe, Stream } from "effect"

const responseSize = Metric.gauge("response_size")
const requestErrors = Metric.counter("request_errors")
const requestDefects = Metric.counter("request_defects")
const rpcSuccesses = Metric.counter("rpc_successes")
const userCount = Metric.gauge("user_count")
const errorsByTag = Metric.frequency("errors_by_tag")
const defectsSeen = Metric.frequency("defects_seen")
const bigintGauge = Metric.gauge("bigint_gauge", { bigint: true })
const metrics = { requests: Metric.counter("requests") }
let mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter")

type Failure = { readonly _tag: "NotFound" } | { readonly _tag: "Timeout" }

declare const handleRequest: Effect.Effect<number, Error>
declare const fetchUsers: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>, Failure>
declare const failsWithString: Effect.Effect<number, string>
declare const bigintEffect: Effect.Effect<bigint>
declare const computeSize: () => number
declare const metricFor: (tag: string) => Metric.Metric<number, Metric.CounterState<number>>

// MUST TRIGGER: issue example, tap / tapError / tapDefect each only update one metric
// tap -> Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize) (input is the parameter verbatim)
// tapError -> Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1) (unused parameter, constant input)
// tapDefect -> Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1)
export const issueExample = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.tap direct-effect overload (Effect-TS/effect rpc-schemas fixture)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const directEffect = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)),
  Fx.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1)
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with a computed input; the input is evaluated
// once when the pipeline is built in both spellings, so withConstantInput keeps that
export const directEffectComputedInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with an inline metric; it is built once in both spellings
export const directEffectInlineMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(Metric.counter("inline_successes"), 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: input is an expression of the parameter -> mapper overload
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, (users) => users.length)
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag, (error) => error._tag)
export const mapperInput = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap((users) => Metric.update(userCount, users.length)),
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error._tag))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: tapError / tapDefect with the parameter as the input verbatim
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag) / Effect.trackDefects(defectsSeen, ...)
export const errorVerbatim = failsWithString.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error))
)
export const defectMapped = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapDefect((defect) => Metric.update(defectsSeen, String(defect)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: constant input computed per run; the mapper form keeps per-run evaluation
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, () => computeSize())
export const perRunConstantInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: ignored but named parameter
export const ignoredParameter = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((_) => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: destructured parameter; the mapper keeps the parameter list
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, ({ length }) => length)
export const destructuredParameter = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap(({ length }) => Metric.update(userCount, length))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: bigint gauge fed with the success value verbatim
export const bigintVerbatim = bigintEffect.pipe(
  Effect.tap((value) => Metric.update(bigintGauge, value))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: block body with a single return of the metric update
export const blockBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    return Metric.update(responseSize, size)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: function expression callback
export const functionExpression = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapError(function() {
    return Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized callback body
export const parenthesizedBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => (Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe function form
export const piped = pipe(handleRequest, Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first forms (callback and direct effect)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(handleRequest, responseSize)
export const dataFirst = Effect.tap(handleRequest, (size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const dataFirstDirect = Effect.tap(handleRequest, Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const dataFirstError = Effect.tapError(handleRequest, () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-last form applied directly
export const dataLast = Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))(handleRequest)

// MUST TRIGGER: aliased module imports for both Effect and Metric
export const aliasedModules = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.tap((size) => M.update(responseSize, size)),
  Fx.tapDefect(() => M.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the API references are hidden behind const aliases
const tapAlias = Effect.tap
const updateAlias = Metric.update
export const aliasedApis = handleRequest.pipe(tapAlias((size) => updateAlias(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable arguments of Effect.fn
export const tracedHandler = Effect.fn("tracedHandler")(
  function*(id: string) {
    return id.length
  },
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: only the metric tap in a longer chain is reported
export const chained = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.map((size) => size * 2),
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.log(size))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a function body, with module-level metrics declared before it
export function nestedScope() {
  return handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already using the track* combinators
export const alreadyTracked = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize),
  Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1),
  Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1),
  Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the callback does more than update one metric
export const alsoLogs = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.log(size))))
)
export const sequencedUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Effect.andThen(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1), Metric.update(userCount, 1)))
)
export const allUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.all([Metric.update(responseSize, size), Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)]))
)
export const delayedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.delay("1 second")))
)
export const multiStatementBlock = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    const doubled = size * 2
    return Metric.update(responseSize, doubled)
  })
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is conditional
export const conditionalUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => size > 0 ? Metric.update(responseSize, size) : Effect.void)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is wrapped in another effect constructor
export const suspendedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.suspend(() => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric depends on the callback parameter
export const metricFromError = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(metricFor(error._tag), 1))
)
export const metricWithErrorAttributes = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(Metric.withAttributes(requestErrors, { tag: error._tag }), 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: inside a callback the metric expression is evaluated on every run;
// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(metrics.requests, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric is declared after the call; the lazy callback reads it
// later, but track* would read it while it is still in the TDZ
export const laterMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(declaredLater, 1))
)
const declaredLater = Metric.counter("declared_later")

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Metric.modify adds a delta and is not what track* calls
export const modifyGauge = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.modify(userCount, size))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: reading a metric value is not an update
export const readMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.value(responseSize))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: data-last Metric.update is out of scope; only the data-first call is matched
export const dataLastUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => responseSize.pipe(Metric.update(size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the direct effect is a precomputed update, not an inline Metric.update call
const precomputedUpdate = Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)
export const precomputedDirect = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(precomputedUpdate))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free callback, not an inline metric update
const recordSize = (size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)
export const pointFree = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(recordSize))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: tap variants without a track* counterpart
export const tapCause = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapCause(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
export const tapErrorTag = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapErrorTag("NotFound", () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)
export const onExit = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.onExit(() => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.tap is a different API
export const streamTap = Stream.make(1, 2, 3).pipe(Stream.tap((n) => Metric.update(responseSize, n)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: unrelated tap/update APIs with the same shape
const unrelated = {
  tap: <A>(f: (a: A) => unknown) => f,
  update: (_metric: unknown, _input: number) => Effect.void
}
export const unrelatedTap = unrelated.tap((size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const unrelatedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap((size) => unrelated.update(responseSize, size)))

void (mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter_2"))

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics manualMetricTapToTrack:warning
import * as Fx from "effect/Effect"
import * as M from "effect/Metric"
import { Effect, Metric, pipe, Stream } from "effect"

const responseSize = Metric.gauge("response_size")
const requestErrors = Metric.counter("request_errors")
const requestDefects = Metric.counter("request_defects")
const rpcSuccesses = Metric.counter("rpc_successes")
const userCount = Metric.gauge("user_count")
const errorsByTag = Metric.frequency("errors_by_tag")
const defectsSeen = Metric.frequency("defects_seen")
const bigintGauge = Metric.gauge("bigint_gauge", { bigint: true })
const metrics = { requests: Metric.counter("requests") }
let mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter")

type Failure = { readonly _tag: "NotFound" } | { readonly _tag: "Timeout" }

declare const handleRequest: Effect.Effect<number, Error>
declare const fetchUsers: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>, Failure>
declare const failsWithString: Effect.Effect<number, string>
declare const bigintEffect: Effect.Effect<bigint>
declare const computeSize: () => number
declare const metricFor: (tag: string) => Metric.Metric<number, Metric.CounterState<number>>

// MUST TRIGGER: issue example, tap / tapError / tapDefect each only update one metric
// tap -> Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize) (input is the parameter verbatim)
// tapError -> Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1) (unused parameter, constant input)
// tapDefect -> Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1)
export const issueExample = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.tap direct-effect overload (Effect-TS/effect rpc-schemas fixture)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const directEffect = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with a computed input; the input is evaluated
// once when the pipeline is built in both spellings, so withConstantInput keeps that
export const directEffectComputedInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with an inline metric; it is built once in both spellings
export const directEffectInlineMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.trackSuccesses(M.withConstantInput(Metric.counter("inline_successes"), 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: input is an expression of the parameter -> mapper overload
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, (users) => users.length)
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag, (error) => error._tag)
export const mapperInput = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap((users) => Metric.update(userCount, users.length)),
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error._tag))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: tapError / tapDefect with the parameter as the input verbatim
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag) / Effect.trackDefects(defectsSeen, ...)
export const errorVerbatim = failsWithString.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error))
)
export const defectMapped = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapDefect((defect) => Metric.update(defectsSeen, String(defect)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: constant input computed per run; the mapper form keeps per-run evaluation
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, () => computeSize())
export const perRunConstantInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: ignored but named parameter
export const ignoredParameter = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((_) => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: destructured parameter; the mapper keeps the parameter list
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, ({ length }) => length)
export const destructuredParameter = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap(({ length }) => Metric.update(userCount, length))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: bigint gauge fed with the success value verbatim
export const bigintVerbatim = bigintEffect.pipe(
  Effect.tap((value) => Metric.update(bigintGauge, value))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: block body with a single return of the metric update
export const blockBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    return Metric.update(responseSize, size)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: function expression callback
export const functionExpression = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapError(function() {
    return Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized callback body
export const parenthesizedBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => (Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe function form
export const piped = pipe(handleRequest, Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first forms (callback and direct effect)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(handleRequest, responseSize)
export const dataFirst = Effect.tap(handleRequest, (size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const dataFirstDirect = Effect.tap(handleRequest, Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const dataFirstError = Effect.tapError(handleRequest, () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-last form applied directly
export const dataLast = Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))(handleRequest)

// MUST TRIGGER: aliased module imports for both Effect and Metric
export const aliasedModules = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.tap((size) => M.update(responseSize, size)),
  Fx.tapDefect(() => M.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the API references are hidden behind const aliases
const tapAlias = Effect.tap
const updateAlias = Metric.update
export const aliasedApis = handleRequest.pipe(tapAlias((size) => updateAlias(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable arguments of Effect.fn
export const tracedHandler = Effect.fn("tracedHandler")(
  function*(id: string) {
    return id.length
  },
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: only the metric tap in a longer chain is reported
export const chained = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.map((size) => size * 2),
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.log(size))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a function body, with module-level metrics declared before it
export function nestedScope() {
  return handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already using the track* combinators
export const alreadyTracked = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize),
  Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1),
  Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1),
  Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the callback does more than update one metric
export const alsoLogs = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.log(size))))
)
export const sequencedUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Effect.andThen(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1), Metric.update(userCount, 1)))
)
export const allUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.all([Metric.update(responseSize, size), Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)]))
)
export const delayedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.delay("1 second")))
)
export const multiStatementBlock = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    const doubled = size * 2
    return Metric.update(responseSize, doubled)
  })
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is conditional
export const conditionalUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => size > 0 ? Metric.update(responseSize, size) : Effect.void)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is wrapped in another effect constructor
export const suspendedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.suspend(() => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric depends on the callback parameter
export const metricFromError = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(metricFor(error._tag), 1))
)
export const metricWithErrorAttributes = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(Metric.withAttributes(requestErrors, { tag: error._tag }), 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: inside a callback the metric expression is evaluated on every run;
// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(metrics.requests, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric is declared after the call; the lazy callback reads it
// later, but track* would read it while it is still in the TDZ
export const laterMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(declaredLater, 1))
)
const declaredLater = Metric.counter("declared_later")

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Metric.modify adds a delta and is not what track* calls
export const modifyGauge = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.modify(userCount, size))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: reading a metric value is not an update
export const readMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.value(responseSize))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: data-last Metric.update is out of scope; only the data-first call is matched
export const dataLastUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => responseSize.pipe(Metric.update(size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the direct effect is a precomputed update, not an inline Metric.update call
const precomputedUpdate = Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)
export const precomputedDirect = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(precomputedUpdate))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free callback, not an inline metric update
const recordSize = (size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)
export const pointFree = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(recordSize))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: tap variants without a track* counterpart
export const tapCause = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapCause(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
export const tapErrorTag = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapErrorTag("NotFound", () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)
export const onExit = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.onExit(() => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.tap is a different API
export const streamTap = Stream.make(1, 2, 3).pipe(Stream.tap((n) => Metric.update(responseSize, n)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: unrelated tap/update APIs with the same shape
const unrelated = {
  tap: <A>(f: (a: A) => unknown) => f,
  update: (_metric: unknown, _input: number) => Effect.void
}
export const unrelatedTap = unrelated.tap((size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const unrelatedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap((size) => unrelated.update(responseSize, size)))

void (mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter_2"))

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics manualMetricTapToTrack:warning
import * as Fx from "effect/Effect"
import * as M from "effect/Metric"
import { Effect, Metric, pipe, Stream } from "effect"

const requestErrors = Metric.counter("request_errors")

const errorsByTag = Metric.frequency("errors_by_tag")

const bigintGauge = Metric.gauge("bigint_gauge", { bigint: true })

// tap -> Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize) (input is the parameter verbatim)

// tapDefect -> Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1)
export const issueExample = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.tap direct-effect overload (Effect-TS/effect rpc-schemas fixture)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const directEffect = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// once when the pipeline is built in both spellings, so withConstantInput keeps that

  Effect.tap(Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

  Effect.tap(Metric.update(Metric.counter("inline_successes"), 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: input is an expression of the parameter -> mapper overload
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, (users) => users.length)
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag, (error) => error._tag)

  Effect.tap((users) => Metric.update(userCount, users.length)),
  Fx.trackErrors(errorsByTag, error => error._tag)

export const errorVerbatim = failsWithString.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error))

  Effect.tapDefect((defect) => Metric.update(defectsSeen, String(defect)))

// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, () => computeSize())
export const perRunConstantInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: ignored but named parameter
export const ignoredParameter = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((_) => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: destructured parameter; the mapper keeps the parameter list
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, ({ length }) => length)
export const destructuredParameter = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap(({ length }) => Metric.update(userCount, length))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: bigint gauge fed with the success value verbatim
export const bigintVerbatim = bigintEffect.pipe(
  Effect.tap((value) => Metric.update(bigintGauge, value))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: block body with a single return of the metric update
export const blockBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    return Metric.update(responseSize, size)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: function expression callback
export const functionExpression = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapError(function() {
    return Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized callback body
export const parenthesizedBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => (Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe function form
export const piped = pipe(handleRequest, Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first forms (callback and direct effect)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(handleRequest, responseSize)
export const dataFirst = Effect.tap(handleRequest, (size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const dataFirstDirect = Effect.tap(handleRequest, Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const dataFirstError = Effect.tapError(handleRequest, () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-last form applied directly
export const dataLast = Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))(handleRequest)

// MUST TRIGGER: aliased module imports for both Effect and Metric
export const aliasedModules = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.tap((size) => M.update(responseSize, size)),
  Fx.tapDefect(() => M.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the API references are hidden behind const aliases
const tapAlias = Effect.tap
const updateAlias = Metric.update
export const aliasedApis = handleRequest.pipe(tapAlias((size) => updateAlias(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable arguments of Effect.fn
export const tracedHandler = Effect.fn("tracedHandler")(
  function*(id: string) {
    return id.length
  },
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: only the metric tap in a longer chain is reported
export const chained = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.map((size) => size * 2),
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.log(size))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a function body, with module-level metrics declared before it
export function nestedScope() {
  return handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already using the track* combinators
export const alreadyTracked = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize),
  Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1),
  Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1),
  Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the callback does more than update one metric
export const alsoLogs = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.log(size))))
)
export const sequencedUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Effect.andThen(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1), Metric.update(userCount, 1)))
)
export const allUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.all([Metric.update(responseSize, size), Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)]))
)
export const delayedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.delay("1 second")))
)
export const multiStatementBlock = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    const doubled = size * 2
    return Metric.update(responseSize, doubled)
  })
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is conditional
export const conditionalUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => size > 0 ? Metric.update(responseSize, size) : Effect.void)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is wrapped in another effect constructor
export const suspendedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.suspend(() => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric depends on the callback parameter
export const metricFromError = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(metricFor(error._tag), 1))
)
export const metricWithErrorAttributes = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(Metric.withAttributes(requestErrors, { tag: error._tag }), 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: inside a callback the metric expression is evaluated on every run;
// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(metrics.requests, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric is declared after the call; the lazy callback reads it
// later, but track* would read it while it is still in the TDZ
export const laterMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(declaredLater, 1))
)
const declaredLater = Metric.counter("declared_later")

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Metric.modify adds a delta and is not what track* calls
export const modifyGauge = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.modify(userCount, size))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: reading a metric value is not an update
export const readMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.value(responseSize))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: data-last Metric.update is out of scope; only the data-first call is matched
export const dataLastUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => responseSize.pipe(Metric.update(size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the direct effect is a precomputed update, not an inline Metric.update call
const precomputedUpdate = Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)
export const precomputedDirect = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(precomputedUpdate))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free callback, not an inline metric update
const recordSize = (size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)
export const pointFree = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(recordSize))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: tap variants without a track* counterpart
export const tapCause = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapCause(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
export const tapErrorTag = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapErrorTag("NotFound", () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)
export const onExit = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.onExit(() => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.tap is a different API
export const streamTap = Stream.make(1, 2, 3).pipe(Stream.tap((n) => Metric.update(responseSize, n)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: unrelated tap/update APIs with the same shape
const unrelated = {
  tap: <A>(f: (a: A) => unknown) => f,
  update: (_metric: unknown, _input: number) => Effect.void
}
export const unrelatedTap = unrelated.tap((size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const unrelatedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap((size) => unrelated.update(responseSize, size)))

void (mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter_2"))

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics manualMetricTapToTrack:warning
import * as Fx from "effect/Effect"
import * as M from "effect/Metric"
import { Effect, Metric, pipe, Stream } from "effect"

const responseSize = Metric.gauge("response_size")
const requestErrors = Metric.counter("request_errors")
const requestDefects = Metric.counter("request_defects")
const rpcSuccesses = Metric.counter("rpc_successes")
const userCount = Metric.gauge("user_count")
const errorsByTag = Metric.frequency("errors_by_tag")
const defectsSeen = Metric.frequency("defects_seen")
const bigintGauge = Metric.gauge("bigint_gauge", { bigint: true })
const metrics = { requests: Metric.counter("requests") }
let mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter")

type Failure = { readonly _tag: "NotFound" } | { readonly _tag: "Timeout" }

declare const handleRequest: Effect.Effect<number, Error>
declare const fetchUsers: Effect.Effect<ReadonlyArray<string>, Failure>
declare const failsWithString: Effect.Effect<number, string>
declare const bigintEffect: Effect.Effect<bigint>
declare const computeSize: () => number
declare const metricFor: (tag: string) => Metric.Metric<number, Metric.CounterState<number>>

// MUST TRIGGER: issue example, tap / tapError / tapDefect each only update one metric
// tap -> Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize) (input is the parameter verbatim)
// tapError -> Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1) (unused parameter, constant input)
// tapDefect -> Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1)
export const issueExample = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: Effect.tap direct-effect overload (Effect-TS/effect rpc-schemas fixture)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const directEffect = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)),
  Effect.tapDefect(() => Metric.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with a computed input; the input is evaluated
// once when the pipeline is built in both spellings, so withConstantInput keeps that
export const directEffectComputedInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct-effect overload with an inline metric; it is built once in both spellings
export const directEffectInlineMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(Metric.update(Metric.counter("inline_successes"), 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: input is an expression of the parameter -> mapper overload
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, (users) => users.length)
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag, (error) => error._tag)
export const mapperInput = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap((users) => Metric.update(userCount, users.length)),
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(errorsByTag, error._tag))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: tapError / tapDefect with the parameter as the input verbatim
// -> Effect.trackErrors(errorsByTag) / Effect.trackDefects(defectsSeen, ...)
export const errorVerbatim = failsWithString.pipe(
  Fx.trackErrors(errorsByTag)
)
export const defectMapped = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapDefect((defect) => Metric.update(defectsSeen, String(defect)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: constant input computed per run; the mapper form keeps per-run evaluation
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, () => computeSize())
export const perRunConstantInput = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(userCount, computeSize()))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: ignored but named parameter
export const ignoredParameter = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((_) => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: destructured parameter; the mapper keeps the parameter list
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(userCount, ({ length }) => length)
export const destructuredParameter = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tap(({ length }) => Metric.update(userCount, length))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: bigint gauge fed with the success value verbatim
export const bigintVerbatim = bigintEffect.pipe(
  Effect.tap((value) => Metric.update(bigintGauge, value))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: block body with a single return of the metric update
export const blockBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    return Metric.update(responseSize, size)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: function expression callback
export const functionExpression = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tapError(function() {
    return Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: parenthesized callback body
export const parenthesizedBody = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => (Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipe function form
export const piped = pipe(handleRequest, Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first forms (callback and direct effect)
// -> Effect.trackSuccesses(handleRequest, responseSize)
export const dataFirst = Effect.tap(handleRequest, (size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const dataFirstDirect = Effect.tap(handleRequest, Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1))
export const dataFirstError = Effect.tapError(handleRequest, () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))

// MUST TRIGGER: data-last form applied directly
export const dataLast = Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))(handleRequest)

// MUST TRIGGER: aliased module imports for both Effect and Metric
export const aliasedModules = handleRequest.pipe(
  Fx.tap((size) => M.update(responseSize, size)),
  Fx.tapDefect(() => M.update(requestDefects, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the API references are hidden behind const aliases
const tapAlias = Effect.tap
const updateAlias = Metric.update
export const aliasedApis = handleRequest.pipe(tapAlias((size) => updateAlias(responseSize, size)))

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable arguments of Effect.fn
export const tracedHandler = Effect.fn("tracedHandler")(
  function*(id: string) {
    return id.length
  },
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: only the metric tap in a longer chain is reported
export const chained = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.map((size) => size * 2),
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)),
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.log(size))
)

// MUST TRIGGER: inside a function body, with module-level metrics declared before it
export function nestedScope() {
  return handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapError(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: already using the track* combinators
export const alreadyTracked = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.trackSuccesses(responseSize),
  Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1),
  Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1),
  Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the callback does more than update one metric
export const alsoLogs = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.log(size))))
)
export const sequencedUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Effect.andThen(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1), Metric.update(userCount, 1)))
)
export const allUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.all([Metric.update(responseSize, size), Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)]))
)
export const delayedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.delay("1 second")))
)
export const multiStatementBlock = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    const doubled = size * 2
    return Metric.update(responseSize, doubled)
  })
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is conditional
export const conditionalUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => size > 0 ? Metric.update(responseSize, size) : Effect.void)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is wrapped in another effect constructor
export const suspendedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.suspend(() => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric depends on the callback parameter
export const metricFromError = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(metricFor(error._tag), 1))
)
export const metricWithErrorAttributes = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(Metric.withAttributes(requestErrors, { tag: error._tag }), 1))

// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(

  Effect.trackErrors(requestErrors, () => 1),
  Effect.trackDefects(requestDefects, () => 1),
  Effect.trackSuccesses(Metric.withConstantInput(rpcSuccesses, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the callback does more than update one metric
export const alsoLogs = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.andThen(Effect.log(size))))
)
export const sequencedUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Effect.andThen(Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1), Metric.update(userCount, 1)))
)
export const allUpdates = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.all([Metric.update(responseSize, size), Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)]))
)
export const delayedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.update(responseSize, size).pipe(Effect.delay("1 second")))
)
export const multiStatementBlock = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => {
    const doubled = size * 2
    return Metric.update(responseSize, doubled)
  })
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is conditional
export const conditionalUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => size > 0 ? Metric.update(responseSize, size) : Effect.void)
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the update is wrapped in another effect constructor
export const suspendedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Effect.suspend(() => Metric.update(responseSize, size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric depends on the callback parameter
export const metricFromError = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(metricFor(error._tag), 1))
)
export const metricWithErrorAttributes = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapError((error) => Metric.update(Metric.withAttributes(requestErrors, { tag: error._tag }), 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: inside a callback the metric expression is evaluated on every run;
// track* evaluates it once, so only stable metric references are safe to move
export const inlineMetricPerRun = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(Metric.counter("per_run"), 1))
)
export const mutableMetricBinding = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(mutableCounter, 1))
)
export const metricPropertyAccess = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(metrics.requests, 1))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the metric is declared after the call; the lazy callback reads it
// later, but track* would read it while it is still in the TDZ
export const laterMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.update(declaredLater, 1))
)
const declaredLater = Metric.counter("declared_later")

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Metric.modify adds a delta and is not what track* calls
export const modifyGauge = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => Metric.modify(userCount, size))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: reading a metric value is not an update
export const readMetric = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap(() => Metric.value(responseSize))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: data-last Metric.update is out of scope; only the data-first call is matched
export const dataLastUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(
  Effect.tap((size) => responseSize.pipe(Metric.update(size)))
)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the direct effect is a precomputed update, not an inline Metric.update call
const precomputedUpdate = Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)
export const precomputedDirect = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(precomputedUpdate))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: point-free callback, not an inline metric update
const recordSize = (size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size)
export const pointFree = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap(recordSize))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: tap variants without a track* counterpart
export const tapCause = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tapCause(() => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1)))
export const tapErrorTag = fetchUsers.pipe(
  Effect.tapErrorTag("NotFound", () => Metric.update(requestErrors, 1))
)
export const onExit = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.onExit(() => Metric.update(rpcSuccesses, 1)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Stream.tap is a different API
export const streamTap = Stream.make(1, 2, 3).pipe(Stream.tap((n) => Metric.update(responseSize, n)))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: unrelated tap/update APIs with the same shape
const unrelated = {
  tap: <A>(f: (a: A) => unknown) => f,
  update: (_metric: unknown, _input: number) => Effect.void
}
export const unrelatedTap = unrelated.tap((size: number) => Metric.update(responseSize, size))
export const unrelatedUpdate = handleRequest.pipe(Effect.tap((size) => unrelated.update(responseSize, size)))

void (mutableCounter = Metric.counter("mutable_counter_2"))
